summary: Tested the tenant lifecycle (create with auto ID, mandatory initial password, delete) on the backend and in the UI. New file test_iter14_tenant_lifecycle.py: 10/10 pass. Creating a FULL tenant produces an ID matching tenant-<16 hex>, quota 5, status ACTIVE, the CUI in uppercase, exactly 1 main branch and a TENANT_ADMIN. The admin has must_change_password=true, a $2b$ bcrypt hash, is assigned to the main branch and has no platform_role. BASIC gets quota 1, and adding a second branch returns 403. Validations: plan GOLD gives 400; a duplicate CUI (case-insensitive) gives 400; a duplicate admin email (case-insensitive) gives 400; a short password gives 422; an email without a password gives 400 and nothing is persisted. The demo admin (not SUPERADMIN) gets 403 on both create and delete. Initial login works and /auth/me returns must_change_password=true. /clients, /vehicles, /work-orders, /dashboard, /users and /platform/tenants all return 403 until the password is changed, using either a Bearer token or cookies only. change-initial-password: wrong current password gives 401, same password gives 400, short password gives 400, no auth gives 401. The correct change returns 200 with a new token and the hash is not exposed. After that /clients returns 200 and is empty (isolated), a second change gives 400, the old password gives 401 and the new one works. Delete: the SUPERADMIN's own active tenant gives 400; an unknown ID gives 404; wrong case in the confirmation gives 400; a missing body gives 422. An exact confirmation (whitespace trimmed) gives 200 and removes the tenant, users, branches, counters and every OPERATIONAL_COLLECTIONS document (including a client created through the API). The deleted admin's old session then gets 401/403. Regression (test_multitenant, test_tenancy, iter12, iter13): 57/57 pass after I updated the old fixtures to the new create schema (cui now required). UI at 390px: scrollWidth is 390; the create panel has exactly 4 inputs and 1 select (company, CUI, email, password, plan) and no tenant ID input; the button is disabled when fields are empty or the password is short. Tenant created as FULL/5 and shown in the list. Admin login redirects to /change-initial-password, and navigating to /clients redirects back. The mismatch, wrong-current and same-password errors all display. The Ieșire (logout) button works. After a successful save the user lands on the dashboard with a toast and /clients is accessible. Delete dialog: the own tenant's button is disabled; confirm is disabled when the input is empty or the case is wrong; Cancel closes the dialog and the input is reset on reopen; an exact name deletes the row and the tenant disappears from the API list. DB check shows 0 leftover data for the UI tenant. No page errors.

minor.issue: The counters cleanup builds the regex f'^{tenant_id}:' without re.escape. TenantIn still accepts an optional custom tenant_id (only a 3-80 char length check). A SUPERADMIN-created ID that contains regex metacharacters, e.g. '(.*)', would wipe ALL tenants' counters when that tenant is deleted. Fix: use re.escape(tenant_id), and either remove tenant_id from TenantIn or restrict it to a pattern such as ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$.

admin_email and initial_password are still optional in the API, so a tenant can be created without an admin or main branch. admin_email is not validated as an email (plain str). The requirement says all 5 fields are mandatory, but only the UI enforces this.

Returns user_out(updated), which does not include the enriched /auth/me fields (branches, platform_role normalisation). The frontend calls setUser(data.user), so the branch switcher and context data may be incomplete until the next /auth/me reload. Consider returning the same payload as /auth/me.

action_items: Use re.escape(tenant_id) in the delete_tenant counters regex, and drop or validate the custom tenant_id field in TenantIn.
Make admin_email (EmailStr) and initial_password required in TenantIn so the API matches the requirement.
Optional: return the /auth/me-equivalent user from change-initial-password (including branches).
critical_code_review_comments: delete_tenant runs several delete_many calls without a transaction. A failure partway through leaves a partially deleted tenant, although the tenant doc is deleted last so a retry is possible. Acceptable, but worth noting.
change-initial-password has no attempt throttling for wrong current passwords. Low risk because the caller is already authenticated with that password.
